# Appeal of Denial — Hip Arthroscopy (CPT 29914)

**[Taylor Kimura]**
**[Street Address]**
**[City, State ZIP]**
**[Phone Number]**
**[Email Address]**

**Date:** [Date of Letter]

**To:** Cigna Appeals Department
**Re:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
**Member:** Taylor Kimura
**Member ID:** W354999576
**Reference Number:** POC-37F3AA304D-16940
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-07-31
**Procedure:** Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
**Governing Policy:** Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 (https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-314%20Hip%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf), effective 2026-08-04

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am writing to ask for a reconsideration of the denial of hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), which I received in a notice dated 2026-07-31. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the records already submitted meet the plan's own published criteria for this surgery.

## Why I believe the records support this surgery

The governing policy states that "femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

The policy further specifies that these criteria include "positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation) ◦ limited passive hip internal rotation • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated):"

Here is how my records match these requirements:

- **Groin-dominant hip pain with provocative testing:** My exam notes document sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and range of motion limited by pain.
- **Failure of non-surgical management for at least three months:** I completed 16 weeks (2026-02-23 to 2026-06-15) of supervised physical therapy — 24 visits — focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also tried NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-21 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. This is well beyond the three-month period described in the policy.
- **Imaging findings:** My MRI arthrogram from 2026-06-24 shows an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees, with joint space preserved and Tonnis grade 0.

The policy also states that FAI surgery "is considered not medically necessary for ANY other indication or condition, including ANY of the following radiographic findings." My imaging shows preserved joint space and Tonnis grade 0, which I understand to reflect early-stage disease consistent with surgical candidacy rather than the advanced findings this exclusion appears to address. If Cigna's determination relied on this exclusion, I would appreciate clarification of which specific radiographic finding was considered disqualifying, since my MRI report does not appear to show one.

I have not requested and am not seeking synovectomy, in-office diagnostic arthroscopy, capsular plication, or anterior inferior iliac spine/subspinous decompression, so I do not believe the policy's separate exclusions for those items apply to my case.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Cigna to review the physical therapy discharge note, the medication and injection records, the exam findings, and the MRI arthrogram report already submitted with the prior authorization request, and to reconsider the denial in light of how these records match the plan's own medical necessity criteria above. If any specific document or data point is still considered missing, I would appreciate a clear, itemized list so that my surgeon's office and I can supply it promptly.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-27. I plan to submit it online at my.cigna.com, and I understand I can also call 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my member ID card with questions. I will use the specific appeal mailing address printed on my denial letter if submitting by mail.

Thank you for reconsidering my request. Please let me know if you need any additional information.

Sincerely,

**[Taylor Kimura]**
**[Signature]**
**[Date]**

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
